findings.statement: CXCR2 (rank one in convergence) is made almost entirely by neutrophils in inflamed mucosa, with a neutrophil share of [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]. In Smillie, where neutrophils were not captured, the attribution lands on T/NK cells and does not replicate in the second dataset (myeloid), so that attribution is an artefact. After composition adjustment the bulk increase keeps only a small part of its size, with a retained fraction of [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17] (verdict partly_composition). It is mainly a marker of neutrophil influx, and a drug would act on neutrophil recruitment.

CXCR1 is a neutrophil gene in the Gubatan data, with a neutrophil share of [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]. The Smillie attribution (T/NK) does not replicate in the second dataset (myeloid), because Smillie lacks neutrophils. Its bulk rise should be read as neutrophil arrival.

CXCL8 is the one leading candidate whose bulk increase is classed as composition: after adjustment the change is no longer significant, with an adjusted padj of [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0527]. In Smillie it is made by macrophages and the myeloid attribution replicates in the second dataset, but neutrophils make a further share of [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]. Adjustment can over-correct when resident myeloid cells become activated, so this is not proof of pure influx.

S100A8 is a myeloid gene that replicates across datasets, and neutrophils make a share of [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909] of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts. The bulk rise partly survives adjustment (verdict partly_composition, adjusted log2FC [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]), so it reports both neutrophil influx and myeloid activation and suits a biomarker role more than a cell-specific target.

MMP1 is made by stromal cells, mainly inflammatory fibroblasts, with a stromal lineage share of [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]. This replicates in the second dataset, and neutrophils contribute little. The bulk change stays significant after composition adjustment, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636], so it is a change inside the tissue and a fibroblast-targeted candidate.

DUOX2 is epithelial, with an epithelial lineage share of [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], mainly in enterocytes, and the attribution replicates in the second dataset. The bulk increase remains significant after adjustment, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161], which supports an intrinsic epithelial induction.

IDO1 is made by myeloid cells (macrophages and DC1 in Smillie, and also enterocytes in Gubatan), the attribution replicates, and neutrophils contribute little. The bulk rise partly survives adjustment, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505] (verdict partly_composition), so it is mostly a tissue-intrinsic change.

CD274 (PD-L1) has a mixed source: plasma cells and macrophages in Smillie, neutrophil states in Gubatan, and some enterocytes. The myeloid attribution replicates. The bulk rise stays significant after adjustment, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978] (partly_composition), so it is partly intrinsic and partly cell influx.

OSMR is stromal, with a stromal lineage share of [gene=OSMR; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.907], mainly inflammatory fibroblasts and WNT2B+ fibroblasts, and replicates in the second dataset. It keeps a small but significant adjusted change, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.2528], so the effect is modest and the receptor sits on the tissue side, a stromal target for oncostatin M signalling.

AQP9 is overwhelmingly a neutrophil gene in the Gubatan data (neutrophil share above nine tenths), so its high rank mainly reflects neutrophil influx and it is a marker of neutrophil arrival rather than a tissue target.

caveats: Smillie did not capture neutrophils, so its cluster attribution for neutrophil-derived genes (CXCR2, CXCR1) falls on T/NK cells and does not replicate in the second dataset; the Gubatan neutrophil share is the reliable view for these genes.

The composition adjustment can over-correct, because lineage scores also rise when resident cells are activated; a retained significant change is strong evidence of a tissue change, whereas a lost change is not proof of pure influx.
Transcript shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance, and dissociation protocols enrich some fractions.
Composition and cell-type attribution were checked for a subset of leading candidates only; other ranked genes (CXCL1, MMP3, MMP7, MMP10, CHI3L1, LCN2, SERPINB5) were not examined at cell level.
